finding.claim: deleteAccount never enforces the ownership or admin check: canDelete's boolean result is discarded, so any authenticated user can delete any other user's account by ID (HIGH).
finding.source: Authenticated low-privilege user calling DELETE /accounts/{id} (route comment at line 19) with another user's account ID.

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) entry point
Account a = accounts.get(id) loads the target account without an ownership check
canDelete(u, a) called; boolean result discarded, so no authorization decision is enforced

finding.guards_checked: canDelete logic at src/AccountService.java:10 is correct but its result is ignored at line 22. assertCanDelete (lines 13-17, throws SecurityException) is not called in deleteAccount, unlike closeAccount line 29. No authorization middleware or route guard is visible in the audited directory. Assumptions not verifiable from this file: IDs are enumerable; User.admin() is derived from a server-side session. Validation tier 0.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. canDelete (src/AccountService.java:9-11) is correct, but its boolean is discarded as a bare statement at line 22, so deleteAccount never checks it. assertCanDelete (lines 13-17, throws) is not called from deleteAccount, unlike closeAccount at line 29. The Grep of the directory found no route, filter, interceptor, or @PreAuthorize guard for DELETE /accounts/{id}.
verdict.reason: At src/AccountService.java:22 the result of canDelete(u, a) is discarded, and line 23 calls accounts.remove(id) unconditionally, so any authenticated non-admin user who can reach the DELETE route can delete another user's account by ID. The attacker is a low-privilege authenticated user, which is below the admin power the flaw grants. The only caveat is that the route wiring and any upstream middleware live outside this directory, so the reachability assumption is not verified here.

finding.claim: Destructive account delete and close execute on the existing session alone with no re-authentication step (MEDIUM). Impact is limited to the owner's own account once AUTH-1 is fixed.
finding.source: Attacker holding a stolen or hijacked session for an account owner.

trace.note: deleteAccount entry point; no credential re-entry or step-up check
closeAccount entry point; no credential re-entry or step-up check

finding.guards_checked: Only ownership/admin checks (assertCanDelete at line 29, canDelete). No re-authentication found in these methods. The re-auth check may exist in the caller layer, which is not in the audited directory, so this finding is not fully confirmed.

verdict.guard_found: In closeAccount, assertCanDelete (src/AccountService.java:29, defined at :13-17) is a throwing ownership/admin check, not re-authentication. In deleteAccount, canDelete at src/AccountService.java:22 returns a bool that is discarded as a bare statement, so it is not an effective guard. No re-auth or step-up check exists anywhere under src/ (grep for re-auth/step-up/password/reauthenticate/confirm returned no matches).
verdict.reason: The trace lines at src/AccountService.java:20, :23, :27 and :30 match the claim and no re-auth check exists in src/, but the candidate itself concedes the caller layer outside the audited directory might enforce re-auth, so absence cannot be confirmed; the more serious issue is that src/AccountService.java:22 discards canDelete's result, letting any authenticated user delete any account, which the candidate's claim does not mention.
